panels.name: cell_expression_dotplot
panels.caption: Dot area is the nonzero fraction; color is mean stored log-normalized expression. First 20 declared variable genes (or genes if flags absent). This is descriptive, not a differential marker test.
panels.title: Expression and detection by cluster
panels.why: A cluster average can hide whether most cells or just a small fraction express a gene.
panels.read: Read color as mean expression and dot area as the fraction of cells with a nonzero measurement. These displayed genes are not automatically tested cell-type markers.

panels.name: evidence_heatmap
panels.caption: Rows are aligned across evidence, measured-layer counts and joint BY q. Direction is defined by the declared orientation. Per-layer p values include feature-to-gene aggregation. Hatched gray cells are untestable; pale cells have weak evidence. Colors retain the same direction scale across all displayed assays.
panels.title: Evidence across assays
panels.why: A candidate can look convincing in one assay while being unmeasured or discordant in another.
panels.read: Read each row across assays, then check measured-layer coverage and joint adjusted evidence. Color shows the declared direction; a missing cell is not a negative result.

panels.name: combined_ranking
panels.caption: Orange marks selected genes; point area increases with measured layer count. Untestable rows have no point. Ranking uses raw joint p; the horizontal scale uses BY q.
panels.title: Ranked evidence
panels.why: A prioritized list needs both an evidence scale and an explanation of how much information supports each entry.
panels.read: Use the axis, threshold and size legend together. Prioritization helps choose follow-up candidates; it does not make the candidates experimentally validated.

panels.name: concordance
panels.caption: Counts include all declared genes, without a significance filter. Same direction is not independent replication. Neutral denotes tied directional evidence; not-both includes unmeasured/untestable genes.
panels.title: Agreement between molecular layers
panels.why: Combining assays is more informative when agreement, disagreement and missing evidence remain distinguishable.
panels.read: Compare direction counts with the total declared feature set. Matching directions across assays are not automatically independent confirmations.

panels.name: measurement_patterns
panels.caption: Exclusive measurement patterns preserve the distinction between absence of evidence and evidence of no association. The TSV contains every observed pattern.
panels.title: What was actually measurable?
panels.why: Apparent improvements can arise when an analysis quietly changes which samples or features it includes.
panels.read: Check the measured denominator and missing categories before comparing results. Coverage and eligibility are different from positive biological evidence.

panels.name: rank_sensitivity
panels.caption: Each column removes one assay and holds r fixed. Average ranks handle ties within the same common testable gene set. Positive values indicate a better rank with that assay. This is sensitivity of supplied evidence, not measured predictive gain; eligibility losses are recorded separately.
panels.title: How prioritization changes
panels.why: An additional assay or a different analysis choice is useful when its effect on the follow-up list is visible.
panels.read: Inspect which candidates move and compare their eligibility. Rank movement is meaningful only within the declared comparison set.

panels.name: pathway_evidence
panels.caption: Top 25 by joint p when enabled, otherwise by minimum layer p for display only. Unsigned enrichment is plotted positive regardless of mechanism. All raw p and descriptive scores remain in the TSV.
panels.title: Pathway evidence across assays
panels.why: Different molecular layers can implicate the same process through different genes.
panels.read: Compare pathway support across assays, then inspect coverage and contributing genes. Signed and unsigned upstream tests have different interpretations.

panels.name: pathway_coverage
panels.caption: Gene coverage uses the assay-specific measured background. A large overlap does not itself establish enrichment.
panels.title: What was actually measurable?
panels.why: Apparent improvements can arise when an analysis quietly changes which samples or features it includes.
panels.read: Check the measured denominator and missing categories before comparing results. Coverage and eligibility are different from positive biological evidence.

panels.name: shared_gene_support
panels.caption: Genes supplied by upstream analyses, such as leading-edge genes or ORA hits, are counted once per pathway. Empty contributions mean the upstream test did not supply gene-level support.
panels.title: Genes behind pathway support
panels.why: Two assays can support the same pathway using entirely different genes.
panels.read: Check which genes contribute and whether support is shared across layers before interpreting pathway agreement as a common mechanism.

panels.name: pathway_overlap
panels.caption: Edges join pathways with full-GMT gene-set Jaccard overlap >= 0.25. This shows annotation redundancy, not molecular interactions or independent biological confirmations.
panels.title: Redundancy between pathway annotations
panels.why: Closely overlapping gene sets can make one biological pattern appear to be many separate findings.
panels.read: Edges indicate shared annotation genes at the declared overlap threshold, not regulatory interactions. Use this view to organize related results.

panels.name: pathway_ranking
panels.caption: Point area encodes -log10(FDR q), capped at 16; position and color encode NES. Negative NES means enrichment toward the negative end of the supplied ranking.
panels.title: Ranked evidence
panels.why: A prioritized list needs both an evidence scale and an explanation of how much information supports each entry.
panels.read: Use the axis, threshold and size legend together. Prioritization helps choose follow-up candidates; it does not make the candidates experimentally validated.

panels.name: leading_edge
panels.caption: Blue indicates leading-edge membership; white is absence from that leading edge, not a negative gene effect. The TSV includes all leading-edge genes in the displayed pathways.
panels.title: Genes behind pathway support
panels.why: Two assays can support the same pathway using entirely different genes.
panels.read: Check which genes contribute and whether support is shared across layers before interpreting pathway agreement as a common mechanism.

panels.name: enrichment_curve_1
panels.caption: Native fgsea plotEnrichment output. The TSV records the full ranked universe and set membership; the separate enrichment-curves.pdf retains native vector curves.
panels.title: Where enrichment is concentrated
panels.why: The running score shows which portion of the full gene ranking drives a gene-set result.
panels.read: Read the score peak alongside hit positions and the signed ranking. Enrichment direction refers to that ranking, not proven pathway activation.
